name: learning_reflection
content: Reflect on this completed experience and produce durable learning candidates if warranted.
## Reflection Boundary
{boundary}
## Current Experience
{episode_json}
## Related Recent Experiences
{related_episodes_json}
## Existing Open Learning Candidates
{existing_candidates_json}
## Extra Review Context
{extra_context_json}
## Decision Rules
1. Prefer no-op over weak candidates. The output may contain zero candidates.
2. Ground every candidate in evidence from the current experience or related recent experiences.
3. Use existing candidates to avoid duplicates. If an existing candidate already covers the learning, return no new candidate and explain that in no_op_reason.
4. Memory candidates should be concise and scoped: user-level for explicit durable user preferences/facts/corrections, agent-level or agent_goal-level for project, strategy, or workflow knowledge.

5. For each memory candidate, include `proposed_change.memory` with `scope`, `target_tier`, `operation`, `key`, `value`, `explicit_user_request`, `explicit_user_correction`, and optional `replaces_key`.
6. Set `review_required=false` only for low-risk user-memory candidates grounded in an explicit user request/correction. Inferred preferences and agent/workspace facts should require review.

7. For each evaluation candidate, include `proposed_change.evaluation` with `case_kind`, `priority`, optional `target_agent_id`, optional `focus_area`, `goal`, `failure_mode`, `expected_behavior`, `reproduction_steps`, `success_criteria`, and `source_refs`.

8. Evaluation candidates should be created when the run revealed a missing regression test, a repeated failure mode, weak capability behavior, memory retrieval/consolidation failure, or a meta-harness review gap. They should normally require review.
9. Capability, wrapper, schema, skill, prompt, persona, docs, program, and evaluation candidates are proposals only and should require review unless obviously low-risk documentation.
10. For failed runs, distinguish between a one-off failure and a reusable bug, missing eval, weak guide, or tool friction pattern.
11. For successful runs, create skill/workflow candidates only when the procedure is reusable or repeated in related experiences.
Use the structured output schema. Do not include markdown or prose outside the schema.

variables.name: boundary
variables.description: Where the reflection was triggered, such as task_terminal_execution or chat_turn_completed

variables.name: episode_json
variables.description: Compact JSON summary of the current episode/experience

variables.name: related_episodes_json
variables.description: Compact JSON array of recent related episodes for repeated-pattern detection

variables.name: existing_candidates_json
variables.description: Compact JSON array of existing open learning candidates for duplicate avoidance

variables.name: extra_context_json
variables.description: Optional meta-harness verdict or caller-specific review context
